doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Broadway pit bands with Elliott Lawrence and Thad Jones-Mel Lewis
summary: Shows like Bye Bye Birdie and How to Succeed, then the Vanguard after the show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well the way I got into Broadway shows, I was working with Elliott Lawrence and things were bad for big bands and we were doing just weekends. And finally he said, “I’m going into the theater I’m going to take the band into the theater.” So I said what did I want to do that for, because that was a schlock job in those days. I mean nobody wanted to play in the theater. It was like working in a submarine. But he said we were going to go in and we’d be able to take off and all that, which you weren’t able to do in those days. But he established that and said you can take off.
Oh. You’d just get a sub?

Yeah. So anyway we started with “Bye Bye Birdie.” And we did that for about a year, it was a big hit, and then he says, “we’re going to change shows.” I said, “what do you want to do that for?” It was a big hit. “No I’m going to change shows.” I said, “what are you going to do?” He said, “well we’ve got this guy, Rudy Vallée and he threw out a bunch of names I never heard of, and I said, “what the heck’s the name of the show?” He said, “How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying.” I said, “how are you going to fit it on the marquee?” But it was another hit.
Bobby Morris, Charles Nelson Reilley, all those people. I didn’t know who they were. I mean I knew Rudy Vallée. I said, “you want to work with Rudy Vallée?”
What’s he going to bring his megaphone?

Yeah. No he did a whole line of shows. We worked with Steve and Edie, “The Golden Rainbow,” we worked with Sammy Davis in “The Golden Boy,” a whole bunch of shows. So that was great. Meanwhile we would take off so I was doing Thad Jones-Mel Lewis. You’d finish the show and you’d go down to The Vanguard and play.
Yeah. Oh that must have been great to do a show and then go play with Thad and Mel and let it all hang out. © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
